name: Shipping for euShipments
author: nozzo

sections.description:
Shipping for euShipments connects your WooCommerce store to your euShipments account through the euShipments public API. You need your own euShipments contract and API token.

This is an independent plugin. It is not made, endorsed or supported by euShipments.

At checkout

  • Every courier and delivery type you enable becomes its own shipping option, for example “FAN Courier – to address” and “Sameday – to office / locker”.
  • Shipping price per option: a fixed price, or the price calculated by euShipments for the cart weight and cash on delivery (exchange rate, VAT, markup and rounding are configurable). Optional free shipping over an amount.
  • Office and locker picker with search by city, street or point name. Pickup points are stored in a local table, so the search is fast. With cash on delivery, points that do not accept it are hidden.
  • The chosen point is shown in the order, in My Account and in the e-mails.
  • “Order shipped” e-mail with the courier, waybill number, tracking button and amount to pay on delivery. It is sent automatically when the waybill is created and can be edited in WooCommerce → Settings → Emails.

In wp-admin (menu “EUShipments”)

  • Orders: lists “To ship”, “Shipped” and “All”, bulk waybill creation and label printing.
  • Order box: create a waybill (weight, parcels, cash on delivery, pickup point), print the label (PDF or ZPL), refresh the status, delete the waybill, create a return.
  • Couriers: the list comes from your euShipments account. For each courier and delivery type you set on/off, name at checkout, price, free shipping threshold and position.
  • Return requests: the customer fills in a return form on your site (shortcode [eusl_return_request]): finds the order by number and e-mail or phone, ticks the products, enters an IBAN (checked) and chooses a courier pickup or a drop-off at an office / locker. Nothing is sent to euShipments until you approve the request and click “Create return”. The customer then gets the return waybill by e-mail, with the PDF label attached.
  • Consolidation: one domestic waybill from you to the euShipments hub for several customer shipments packed in one box. Settings are filled in once; the page lists the shipments not yet consolidated, ticked, with the total weight. One click creates the waybill and opens its label. A shipment can be in one consolidation only. Customers and their orders see nothing of it.
  • Automatic: pickup points are refreshed daily, open shipments and returns are tracked every hour, and the order can switch to “Completed” when the parcel is delivered.

Requirements

  • WooCommerce 8.0 or newer, with the classic (shortcode) checkout. The block checkout is not supported yet.
  • An euShipments account and API token.
  • HPOS (High-Performance Order Storage) is supported.

External services

This plugin connects to the euShipments API (operated by euShipments / InOut, https://eushipments.com). Without it the plugin cannot work.

Calls go to https://api1.inout.bg/api/v1/ (or https://test-api.inout.bg/api/v1/ if you choose the test environment). Every call sends your API token.

What is sent and when:

  • When you connect or open the Couriers page: only your API token, to read your companies and couriers.
  • Daily (WP-Cron) and when you click “Sync now”: a request for the list of offices and lockers of your enabled couriers. No customer data is sent.
  • At checkout, when a price is “calculated by euShipments”: your company ID, the courier, the delivery type (address or office), the cart weight, the cash-on-delivery amount and the currency. No customer data is sent.
  • When you create a consolidated waybill: your company ID, the courier, the hub address and phone from the consolidation settings, weight, parcels, a reference and the list of the customer waybill numbers inside. Optionally the same waybill numbers are sent to mark them as expedited. No customer data is sent.
  • When you create a waybill or a return: the data the courier needs to deliver or collect the parcel: customer name, address, postcode, phone, e-mail, chosen pickup point, order number, product names, quantities and prices, weight, parcels, cash-on-delivery amount and the customer note. Your sender name and phone are sent too.
  • When you print a label, refresh a status or delete a waybill: the waybill number.
  • Hourly (WP-Cron): the numbers of open waybills and returns, to read their status.

Return requests and IBANs entered by customers stay in your WordPress database. They are not sent to euShipments.

euShipments privacy policy: https://eushipments.com/privacy-policy
Your terms of use for the API are in your contract with euShipments.

The “Order shipped” e-mail contains a link to the courier’s own tracking page (for example FAN Courier, Sameday, Cargus, GLS or Speedy). Your site does not contact those websites; the customer opens the link.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce.
  2. In wp-admin go to Plugins → Add New, search for “Shipping for euShipments”, click Install, then Activate.
  3. Go to EUShipments → Settings, paste your API token, click “Connect” and choose your company.
  4. Fill in the sender name and phone, weights and box size.
  5. Go to EUShipments → Couriers, enable the couriers and delivery types you want, set the prices and save. Click “Sync now” under each office / locker service.
  6. Go to WooCommerce → Settings → Shipping, open your shipping zone and add the method “EUShipments”.
  7. Optional: create a page with the shortcode [eusl_return_request] for online return requests.
sections.faq:
Do I need an euShipments account?

Yes. The plugin uses your own euShipments contract and API token. Prices and services are the ones in your account.

Does it work with the block checkout?

Not yet. Use the classic checkout page (shortcode [woocommerce_checkout]).

Which couriers are supported?

The ones enabled in your euShipments account. The plugin reads them from the API, so new couriers appear without an update.

Are test waybills charged?

euShipments asks to use the live API. A waybill that is deleted and never handed to the courier is not charged. Check this with euShipments for your contract.

Can a customer return only part of an order?

Yes. On the return form the customer ticks the products and, for lines with more than one piece, the quantity.

Where are the logs?

WooCommerce → Status → Logs, source “eushipments-lite”. Turn on “Log API answers” in the settings for more detail.

I used the older “WooCommerce EUShipments shipping Lite” version. How do I switch?

Settings, couriers and order data are kept, because the new version uses the same option names. Deactivate the old plugin, then activate this one. Do not run both at the same time.
sections.changelog:
1.1.1

  • Consolidation uses the createConsolidatedAWB method: the sender company on the label is your own (“Sender company” setting) and the payer is euShipments, as in the client panel.

1.1.0

  • Consolidation: one domestic waybill to the euShipments hub for several customer shipments, with its own settings, list, label, status and delete. A shipment can be in one consolidation only.
  • Optionally marks the customer waybills as expedited at euShipments.

1.0.0

  • First release on WordPress.org (renamed from “WooCommerce EUShipments shipping Lite” 0.3.0).
  • Partial returns: the customer ticks products and quantities on the return form.
  • Return waybill e-mailed to the customer with the PDF label attached.
  • Security and coding-standard fixes: escaped output, sanitized input, prepared SQL with identifier placeholders, translator comments.
